entities.name: University of Melbourne
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The University of Melbourne, founded in 1853 — is Australia's second oldest university (after the University of Sydney, 1850) and consistently ranked as Australia's top or co-top research university, the flagship institution of the state of Victoria and Australia's cultural capital city. Melbourne was founded just years after Victoria's 1851 gold rush transformed the region from a frontier colony into one of the world's wealthiest cities, and the university's rapid development reflected the new colony's ambitions and wealth.

The University of Melbourne's Parkville campus is architecturally significant: the historic quadrangle buildings in bluestone (a distinctive Melbourne architectural material) represent Victorian-era Australian ambitions to create an institution equivalent to the ancient English universities. The university's growth in the late 19th and early 20th centuries coincided with Melbourne's period as Australia's financial capital and de facto national capital (until Canberra was established in 1927), and many of Australia's most significant 19th-20th century figures — judges, politicians, scientists — were educated there.

Melbourne's academic strength is broad: the faculties of law, medicine, engineering, and the sciences are all nationally premier. Notable alumni include Graeme Clark (inventor of the cochlear implant, a technology that has restored hearing to over 700,000 people globally, one of the most significant medical technology achievements in history), multiple Australian Prime Ministers, and internationally significant scholars. The university's 2008 Melbourne Model restructured undergraduate education to graduate professional schools, influencing Australian higher education broadly.
